name: Richy Design System
description: Premium financial app design system — expensive, warm, understated wealth. Apple-inspired with data-dense Bloomberg terminal aesthetic.

philosophy.feeling: Smart and calm — not stressful, not gamified, not cluttered
philosophy.warmth: Cream tones and warm materials, never gray or sterile white
philosophy.wealth: Like a real wealth tool — the kind a rich person would actually use
philosophy.personality: Personal and conversational — knows your name, greets you like a person
philosophy.density: Numbers ARE the decoration. Typography and data density create richness
philosophy.restraint: Wealth implied by restraint, not decoration. Premium banking meets Bloomberg terminal

principles: NO emojis. Anywhere. Ever. Not in UI, greetings, categories, or copy
Buttons are short: 'Sign In' not 'Click here to sign in'
Greetings are human and casual: 'Good morning, Alon.' NOT exclamatory
Fill space with information and data, not whitespace and decoration
Shadows are barely-there but present — depth reads as substance
borderRadius: 20-22px on everything — generous, Apple-style, never square

purple.description: Lavender hero with violet accents and dark text — default theme

classic.description: Dark hero with warm orange accents and white text — original theme

blue.description: Light wisteria hero with steel-azure accents and dark text, built on the six-step Steel Azure ramp (Floral White #FFF8EE, Alabaster Grey #DEE3E6, Powder Blue #AFC3D5, Wisteria Blue #7AA1CB, Rich Cerulean #3D76AD, Steel Azure #004A8F)

glass.description: iOS 26-style Liquid Glass material system for nav bars and sheets
glass.mechanism: blur + saturate + specular edge (bright inset top) + soft lift shadow

heroCard.description: Centerpiece of the app — premium banking aesthetic

layout.balanceLabel: NET BALANCE — tiny all-caps white/40% opacity
layout.savingsRate: green pill badge if ≥20%, orange otherwise
layout.metrics: Income vs Spent side-by-side with separator

interactions.tapToToggle: Net Worth vs Balance via hero pill interaction
interactions.darkMode: Gradients and text colors adapt via theme system

navBar.glassSpec: inset bright top rim + soft lift shadow
navBar.activeTabs: frosted capsule lens behind selected icon

darkMode.description: Adaptive light/dark mode that respects theme-specific hero colors
darkMode.implementation: applyDarkMode(dark) called on every render, toggles entire glass/nav/sheet system
darkMode.scrimBlur: 4px blur with 120% saturation on dim backdrop
darkMode.navBarBehavior: frosted glass with adaptive rim highlights and specular sheen

doNotChange: Dark hero balance card (classic theme) or light hero gradients (purple/blue themes)
Primary action colors per theme (orange #C8673A classic, purple #8970C6 for violet, steel azure #004A8F for blue)
Apple system font stack (no web fonts)
Bottom tab bar with SVG icons
warnings: Light-hero themes (purple, blue): hero text is dark, not the primary accent color. #004A8F alone is too low-contrast on the wisteria hero — always check contrast when adding new light-hero themes
Liquid glass effect is subtle by design — avoid increasing blur or saturation beyond documented values
Nav bar behavior requires careful shadow and specular rim tuning per light/dark mode to maintain the lens effect

statusBar.light: light content (white text, light icons on dark nav)
statusBar.dark: dark content (dark text, dark icons on light nav)

notes.themeSystem: Themes are runtime-switchable via Profile > Appearance. User choice persisted as 'theme' in Firestore. Three palettes supported: purple (default), classic, blue. Add new themes by extending THEMES object and THEME_LABELS map.
notes.glassSystem: Comprehensive Liquid Glass material system for iOS 26-style nav bar refraction, pill-shaped active-tab lens, frosted sheets, and adaptive light/dark glass tokens. Never apply static 30% opacity to nav bars — use the glass system tokens instead.
notes.darkMode: Full dark mode support via applyDarkMode(). Glass tokens adapt (bright specs in dark, dark borders in light) to maintain visibility.
notes.accessibility: All text has been checked for WCAG contrast. Light-hero themes use darkened ink (e.g., #0B2E52) on hero, not the primary color.
